data.narrative:
Cognitive Space, a Seed-stage Space & Aerospace company founded by Guy de Carufel, has raised $10.3M to date. The broader sector comp universe includes 6 public equities (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) and 8 private peers spanning companies like SpaceX, Rocket Lab, and ICEYE, though the narrow peer set at identical stage and valuation tier remains thin.

Of three valuation methods examined, only stage-progression anchoring is applicable. This method uses the $10.3M capital raised as a proxy for current enterprise value and applies a typical 2.5x step-up multiplier to estimate post-Seed valuation, yielding $25.75M. Public-comp anchoring cannot be applied—while Space & Aerospace public companies trade at a 25.3x median P/S, Cognitive Space's revenue is not on file, precluding revenue-multiple derivation. Peer-median methodology is inapplicable due to insufficient same-stage comparables; only one narrow-filter peer exists within the Space & Aerospace dataset.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $22M to $30M, centered at $26M, derived entirely from stage-progression mechanics. This range should be treated cautiously given reliance on a single method and the absence of revenue visibility. Key uncertainties include the company's revenue run-rate, capital efficiency trajectory, and competitive positioning relative to better-capitalized private peers. Additional financial disclosure or revenue traction would materially sharpen conviction around this estimate.
